chunks: And by this chain, from Muhammad ibn Suleyman, from Ibrahim ibn Abdullah Al-Sufy, who said: Musa ibn Bakr Al-Wasity told me, saying:

Abu Al-Hassan (peace be upon him) said to me: 'If I were to distinguish my Shias, I would not find them except as those who merely describe themselves (talk). And if I were to test them, I would not find them except as apostates. And if I were to scrutinize them, not one out of a thousand would remain pure. And if I were to screen them with a sieve, there would not remain from them except that which was truly mine. Indeed, they have leaned upon their couches for a long time and said,
We are the Shias of Ali.
But rather, the Shia of Ali is the one whose action confirms his word.
ai.seo_question: What is the true definition of a Shia according to Imam Al-Hassan (peace be upon him)?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Al-Kafi, Imam Al-Hassan (AS) employs a rhetorical triad of testing—examination, purification, and sifting—to illustrate the scarcity of true believers among those who merely claim allegiance to Ali (AS). He contrasts the complacency of the 'reclining' masses who rely on self-identification with the rigorous standard of 'Siddiqun' (truthful ones) whose actions perfectly validate their words. This highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on 'Amal' (practice) as the ultimate criterion for distinguishing genuine followers from nominal ones, a concept deeply rooted in the tradition of the Ahl al-Bayt.
